The projects address critical needs in data management, use, standards and mobilization

Four projects have been selected for funding through the 2026 round of the GBIF's annual Capacity Enhancement Support Programme (CESP) call. This programme addresses specific capacity needs identified through the GBIF Participant network at both regional and global levels. The four projects are led by nodes in Oceania, Latin America and the Caribbean and Europe and involve collaborators from all over the world. These projects focus on a variety of topics including increasing capacity of data providers to adopt Darwin Core Data Packages for specimen data, strengthening technical capacity within new nodes, providing guidance and systems for managing restricted access species data and improving data mobilization capacity for eDNA and metabarcoding sampling-event datasets.

Projects were competitively selected by community reviewers and selection panel members from the GBIF volunteer network. To date, more than 60 projects led by 35 countries have received nearly € 900,000 in funding through CESP across its 12-year history.
